items.title: [verbose ci] in the head commit makes a manual CI run verbose
items.description: ### Narrative A commit-message marker such as `[verbose ci]` steers a CI run. Every marker, `[verbose ci]` included, is meant to act on a manual run (`workflow_dispatch`) as well as on push and pull_request. In the consumer template `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml`, the force markers already do. The "Detect Direct Push" step (lines 86-109 and 335-358) reads the PR title on `pull_request` and the head commit with `git log -1 --pretty=%B "$GITHUB_SHA"` on every other event, so `[force cache]`, `[force build]` and `[force full]` work on a manual run. `[verbose ci]` does not. It is read in the job-level `env:` blocks of `bkit-tests-static` (lines 54-57) and `bkit-tests-unit` (lines 311-314) with `contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[verbose ci]') || contains(github.event.pull_request.title, '[verbose ci]')`. A manual run's payload carries neither field, so `VERBOSE_CI`, `TURBO_LOG_LEVEL`, `NODE_OPTIONS` and the `DEBUG` value written by "Configure Verbose CI" all stay off. The comment at template line 926 says the opposite of the decision: "a marker cannot, because markers are inert on workflow_dispatch". `.bkit/core/.bkit/workflows.md:1252` says the same for every marker, which is already wrong for the template's force markers. Once done, a manual run whose head commit carries `[verbose ci]` runs the static and unit lanes with verbose output, the template comment and the workflows doc say markers act on a manual run, and bkit's own adopted copy `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` stays identical to the template. A job-level `env:` cannot run git, so the head commit has to be read by a step. A step can turn `VERBOSE_CI`, `TURBO_LOG_LEVEL` and `DEBUG` on for later steps by writing them to `$GITHUB_ENV`. GitHub refuses `NODE_OPTIONS` from `$GITHUB_ENV`, so `--trace-warnings` stays off on a manual run. ### Success Criteria - On a `workflow_dispatch` run whose head commit message contains `[verbose ci]`, the static and unit jobs of the template run their steps after the marker step with `VERBOSE_CI=1`, `TURBO_LOG_LEVEL=debug` and `DEBUG=vercel:*,supabase:*`. - On a `workflow_dispatch` run whose head commit has no `[verbose ci]`, none of those values is set. - Push and pull_request runs behave exactly as today. - No comment in either CI file and no line of `.bkit/core/.bkit/workflows.md` § Commit-message force tags says a marker is inert on `workflow_dispatch`. - `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` matches the template outside its recorded edits. ###

items.title: Passage search: belief-aware local reranker (sidecar), plus opt-in LLM query expansion
items.description: # Feature Specification: Passage search: belief-aware local reranker (sidecar), plus opt-in LLM query expansion **Feature Branch**: `fabrik/issue-796` **Created**: 2026-11-18 **Status**: Specified **Input**: User description: > ## Problem > > On the v2 retrieval corpus (#788, baseline posted on #789), LCG passage search beats qmd overall: nDCG@10 0.567 vs 0.499, a paired difference of +0.068 [+0.017, +0.116]. It loses badly on **paraphrase** questions, which describe an entity by its role ("the initiative covering shift rostering") without naming it: > > | paraphrase, nDCG@10 | | > |---|---| > | `lcg-passages` | 0.150 | > | `qmd` (hybrid + LLM query expansion) | 0.356 | > | `qmd-rerank` (+ Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B) | **0.492** | > > qmd closes that gap with two stages LCG lacks: > - **LLM query expansion** (`qmd-query-expansion-1.7B`): keyword, semantic and HyDE variants of the query, fused. > - **A cross-encoder reranker** over the top candidates. > > Both are expensive (1.7 s and 3.3 s p50, against LCG's 24 ms). The reranker also wrecks temporal questions: qmd-rerank scores 0.293 there, against 0.628 for `lcg-passages`. It scores text match and is blind to which note is current. > > Real users ask by role and description all the time, so this gap is not just a quirk of the test set. > > ## Desired behaviour > > Two optional stages for passage search, **each one switchable on its own and measured on its own**. > > ### 1. Rerank stage (the primary goal) > - After first-stage retrieval, rescore the top N candidates (N about 20–30, configurable) with a **small local cross-encoder**: a BGE-reranker-base / bge-reranker-v2-m3 class model, or similar. > - Serve it from the Swift local-inference sidecar (`native/local-inference`, CoreML) so that Liminis Notes gets it with no new process. > - LCG reaches it through the existing UDS/HTTP embedder transport pattern, e.g. a `/v1/rerank` route. > - **Belief-aware:** combine the reranker score with LCG's belief and recency signals so the stage cannot repeat qmd's temporal collapse. A superseded note must not climb above the current one on text match alone. > - Budget: p50 total ≤ 150 ms for k = 10 on Apple silicon. > - Off by default until measured. A client opts in per call (`rerank: true`) or through config. > > ### 2. Query expansion (opt-in only) > - Optionally rewrite the query with a local LLM into lexical, semantic and hypothetical-answer variants, and fuse them with RRF. items.description: ## Goal Loop courses on federal land in Virginia, keeping only the distances that make a genuinely good run: - National Park Service units. - National forests (USFS), in their own section. - Wildlife refuges (USFWS), in their own section. Related: - #1430: Richmond area, including Richmond National Battlefield Park (Malvern Hill, Cold Harbor). - #1432: point-to-point and rail-trail courses, including the Mount Vernon Trail and Great Dismal Swamp. - #1433: state parks. - #1431: build tooling, including agency values for USFS and USFWS. ## What "worth running" means here Same rule as #1433: - **Keep rule:** each lap has 15% backtracking or less; a 10K at most 2 laps, a half at most 3, a marathon at most 3 laps of 14 km or more. - **Dropped:** anything that needs more. - **Data:** OSM foot network per unit, with nps.gov and fs.usda.gov rules checked 2026-11-18. - **Climb figures:** from coarse elevation data, so treat them as floors. ## Standout runs 1. **Shenandoah NP, Big Meadows / Skyland marathon:** a single 42.2 km loop, 8% backtracking. A mountain ultra-style course with at least 1,800 m of climb. 2. **Mount Rogers NRA marathon:** a single 42.2 km loop, 0% backtracking, at least 1,250 m of climb (self-guided; see USFS race limits). 3. **Manassas half:** a single 21.1 km loop with 0% backtracking; the marathon is 2 laps of it. (Not built: that loop crosses US-29 and VA-234 at grade; see Skipped.) 4. **Prince William Forest:** a single-lap 10K, a single-lap half, and a 2-lap marathon, no horses. 5. **Pandapas Pond / Poverty Creek half:** a single 21.1 km loop, the most runnable mountain network found. 6. **Shenandoah NP south district (Loft Mountain / Big Run) half:** a single 21.1 km loop. 7. **Theodore Roosevelt Island 5K:** car-free, on a wooded island in the Potomac. ## National Park Service Cells read laps × lap length, backtracking per lap. items.title: Virginia point-to-point and rail-trail courses: half to 100K
items.description: ## Goal Point-to-point and out-and-back courses on Virginia's long linear trails, up to ultra distances. These are the runs no park loop can give: a marathon or 50 mile with no laps. **Blocked on #1431:** point-to-point and out-and-back support, the 50 mile and 100K distances, and modelling a trail that isn't a park. Related: #1430 (Richmond area), #1433 (state parks), #1434 (national parks, forests and refuges). Distances below are measured on the OSM trail line between OSM parking areas within 250 m of the trail. Official mileposts are cross-checked where the trail has them. Data checked 2026-11-18. ## Standout runs 1. **New River Trail, 50 mile:** Galax to Pulaski, 79.9 km, net downhill on cinder. Add a 0.5 km out-and-back to reach 80.5 km. 2. **Virginia Capital Trail, 50 mile:** almost the whole trail, just east of Great Shiplock Park to Jamestown (mile 0), paved. 3. **High Bridge Trail, marathon:** Burkeville-end lot to Elam, 42.5 km, flat crushed limestone across the High Bridge. 4. **W&OD, 50K:** Purcellville to Clarks Crossing (Vienna), 49.95 km, paved, net downhill west to east. 5. **Virginia Creeper, Whitetop to Damascus and on:** about 500 m of continuous descent. Available once the upper section reopens on 2027-03-31; no standard distance lands on a parking lot yet (see below). 6. **Great Dismal Swamp, Washington Ditch:** a straight dirt road to Lake Drummond. items.title: Richmond-area park courses: scouting and build list
items.description: ## Goal **Statewide follow-ups:** #1433 (state parks), #1434 (national parks, forests and refuges), #1432 (point-to-point and rail trails), #1431 (build tooling). This issue keeps the Richmond-area batch, including the smaller city and county parks; smaller parks elsewhere come later. Build out the Richmond-area park course catalogue: 5K, 10K, half and marathon courses in the parks with enough trail. The Virginia Capital Trail's point-to-point and ultra courses moved to #1432. Deep Run Park's 5K (staged, #1097) is the only one so far. This issue is the scouting result and the build list. Each course still goes through the normal `scripts/parks/` flow (OSM ways, `trail_review` against the land manager's map, `fetch_snapshot.mjs`, `build.mjs`, staged release). ## How the routes were found - **Source data:** OpenStreetMap only. Footway, path, track, cycleway and bridleway ways within about 25 km. Excluded: sidewalks (except as short connectors), anything `access=private`, `foot=no` or `informal=yes`, and Pipeline Trail (officially closed). - **Map gaps:** dead ends within 15 m of another trail were joined. Trail pieces close together were linked by mapped sidewalks or bridges (400 m or less, plus the Boulevard Bridge sidewalk). Each one is a likely OSM fix or a check to make. - **Search:** for each distance, try 1 to 4 laps (max 2 for a 10K, 3 for a half, 4 for a marathon). Each lap is the longest no-repeat loop that fits, plus a short spur, or a pruned tour of the network. Keep the fewest laps that stay under the backtracking threshold. - **Rating** (backtracking within one lap): **Build** 15% or less, **Maybe** 30% or less, **Drop** above 30%. Laps in moderation are fine; backtracking inside a lap is what counts against a route. - **Not done yet:** no ground check, and no way-by-way check against each park's own trail map. That's the `trail_review` step. ## Build list ### Virginia Capital Trail Moved to #1432 with the other point-to-point and rail-trail courses (5K to 50 mile). ### James River Park System (Buttermilk, North Bank, Forest Hill, Belle Isle), city of Richmond - [ ] 5K: one 5 km loop, 0% backtracking - [ ] 10K: 2 laps of the 5 km loop. Alternative: the 10.15 km Buttermilk + North Bank short loop, with the finish 150 m before the start. - [ ] Half: one 21.1 km lap of the Buttermilk + North Bank loop, 0% backtracking - [ ] Marathon: 2 laps of the 21.1 km loop, 0% backtracking The big loop is North Bank, Boulevard Bridge, Buttermilk, Forest Hill, t

items.title: AMR follow-ups after #2117 (tracking issue)
items.description: Tracking issue for the open problems and follow-up work for block-structured AMR, which landed in #2117 (merged as eb63cfa5). Each item comes from that PR's *Known limitations and follow-ups* section, plus two caveats noted in the code (the finest-level dt warning and the coarse-only species-cleanup report). Each linked issue gives the current behaviour, the reason, code links pinned to eb63cfa5, what is needed, and when it counts as done. Everything listed is either rejected by the case validator with a message (`toolchain/mfc/case_validator.py`, `check_amr`) or documented as a caveat, so no unsupported input runs silently. User docs: `docs/documentation/amr.md` (*Limitations*); design and the grid-swap contract: `docs/documentation/amr_implementation.md`. ### Open bug - [x] #2217 quartic prolongation (amr_prolong = 2) goes NaN after a regrid in a dense immersed-body cloud ### Performance, memory and code structure - [ ] #2218 regrid cost grows faster than the step beyond 512 GPUs (clustering and global block-table exchange) - [ ] #2219 solver work arrays are sized for the largest block, so every block pays for it (memory headroom) - [ ] #2220 pass the grid to the solver explicitly instead of swapping module-global grid state per block - [ ] #2221 replace m_amr_state's loose module variables with a block-table derived type ### Refinement behaviour - [ ] #2222 refinement never retracts when no cell is tagged (regrid keeps the old blocks) - [ ] #2223 level-2 and deeper blocks are re-prolonged from their parent at every regrid (no carry-over): fix in #2295 - [x] #2245 fine blocks advance at the coarse dt; dt is not limited by the finest cell (multi-level / ratio 4 without subcycling) - [ ] #2244 refinement ratio 4 beyond one level, quartic with ratio 4, subcycling beyond two levels, static nesting beyond level 2 ### Immersed boundaries under AMR - [x] #2224 integrate immersed-boundary forces (face-flux path) on the fine grid, not the coarse grid only - [ ] #2225 moving immersed bodies with amr_max_level > 1 or with amr_subcycle - [ ] #2226 validate IB thermal walls (thermal_bc = 1, 2) and surface reactions (surface_reaction, thermal_layer) - [ ] #2228 lumped solid wall (patch_ib thermal_bc = 3) under AMR - [ ] #2229 support ib_heat_wrt (IB heat output) on refined blocks - [ ] #2227 support ib_surface_wrt (per-ghost-point surface output) on refined blocks - [ ] #2230 support ib_flux_wall (HLLC wall-flux override) on refined blocks - [ ] #2240 STL-model immers

items.title: feat(parks): point-to-point, out-and-back and ultra course support for the course catalogue
items.description: ## Goal The build-tool and model work that the statewide course issues depend on. Today `scripts/parks/build.mjs` builds loop race courses only, the race-distance list stops at 50K, and a course must belong to a park. Needed by: #1430 (Richmond area), #1432 (point-to-point and rail trails), #1433 (state parks), #1434 (national parks, forests and refuges). ## Work - [x] **Point-to-point and out-and-back race courses** in `scripts/parks/build.mjs`. - `course_shape` already allows both; the README says only loops are built so far. - An out-and-back needs a turnaround checkpoint so a short cut can't time. - A point-to-point needs separate start and finish lines. - Needed for every rail-trail course, the Capital Trail and the Great Dismal Swamp ditch road. - [ ] **Add the 50 mile and 100K race distances.** `RACE_DISTANCES_M` (`scripts/parks/lib/course_geometry.mjs`) and the payload labels stop at `50k`. - 50 mile: Capital Trail (point to point, nearly the full trail), New River Trail (Galax to Pulaski) and High Bridge (out and back). - 100K: W&OD and High Bridge, both out and back. - Check every client rail that enumerates race distances (`check_constraint_unions.mjs` will name them if there's a CHECK). - [x] **Model a trail that isn't a park.** The Capital Trail, W&OD, Virginia Creeper, Mount Vernon Trail, Huckleberry and Fall Line are linear trails run by VDOT, NOVA Parks, USFS with towns, NPS, and multi-county partnerships. Decide between a `parks` row (agency `other`) per trail and a separate concept. - [ ] **Agency vocabulary for federal land that isn't NPS.** USFS (George Washington & Jefferson National Forests) and USFWS (wildlife refuges) courses need an `agency` value (`other`, or new `usfs` / `usfws` values) and their own closure and permit notes. The NPS closures sweep doesn't cover them. - [ ] **Harden the foot-access check.** - The build refuses `bicycle=designated` only together with `foot=no`. - At York River State Park, DCR lists John Blair Trail and Bobcat Run as mountain-bike only, but OSM tags them bike-designated with no `foot` tag. - `trail_review` would still catch it (the designated list is manual). Consider making the build at least warn on `bicycle=designated` / `mtb=designated` without explicit foot access. - [ ] **Optional: commit the scouting tool.** - The statewide pass used a scout script that fetches a park's OSM foot network, joins near-miss gaps (15 m) and short sidewalk links (400 m), and picks 5K to marathon routes by the lap/

items.description: ## 목표 moraebot 슬랙 앱을 Slack **agent app**(Agents 기능, 상단 진입점 + 옆 패널 대화)으로 쓸 수 있게 하기. 오너 요청 (2026-11-20, Slack DM): "슬랙 에이전트 모드로 둘다 바꾸기". mori 쪽은 브리지에서 이미 전환함. ## 지금 코드 상태 (main 1b45949 이후) - `src/slack.rs:185-199`: DM(`channel_type == "im"`)과 `thread_ts`를 이미 읽고, 스레드 루트가 아닐 때 ` : `로 대화를 나눔. - 답장은 `post_body(channel, thread_ts, text)`(`src/slack.rs:251`)로 스레드에 넣을 수 있음. ## 필요한 것 1. 매니페스트(`docs/guides/slack-manifest.json`): `features.agent_view`(또는 앱 설정 Agents 토글에 해당하는 키) 켜기, bot scope `assistant:write` 추가, 필요하면 event `assistant_thread_started`. 2. DM이 에이전트 스레드로 들어올 때 **루트 메시지에도 그 메시지 ts로 스레드 답장**하기 (지금은 루트 DM에 스레드 없이 답함). 3. 턴 시작 시 `assistant.threads.setStatus`(또는 `agents.sessions.setStatus` processing → 답장 후 active)로 로딩 표시. 레거시 setStatus는 답장 시 자동으로 꺼짐. 4. (선택) `assistant.threads.setTitle` / `agents.sessions.rename`로 스레드 제목을 첫 메시지 요약으로. 5. 가이드 `docs/guides/slack.md`에 Agents 토글과 재설치 안내. ## 확인 - 무료 플랜에서 Agents 표시가 실제로 되는지는 아직 확인 안 함 (Slack 문서: 일부 AI 기능은 유료 플랜 필요). - 테스트: 루트 DM → 스레드 답장, 스레드 DM → 같은 스레드 답장, setStatus 호출 여부(가짜 Slack API). 참고: https://docs.slack.dev/ai/developing-agents

items.title: 【erp3d】门洞＋关联门板：柜体树门洞辅助层，门板自动适配（酷家乐对齐；重写原方案 B）
items.description: **结论**：把酷家乐「门洞＋关联门板」整套能力搬进编辑器——柜体树上新增可设计的「门洞」辅助层，门板收编为其子节点并自动适配尺寸/位置/开门方向；门洞是影子层，不进生产导出与报价。本单重写自原 #575 方案 B（只代填公式、不建实体）：经 2026-11-16 grill 拍板改为真建门洞层——方案 B 的调研产出全部继承，「代填公式命令」与「存量补挂」作废。 ## ⚠️ 2026-11-19 rework 口径修正（用户拍板，子票 T1–T4） > 本节为**最高口径**，与下文冲突处一律以本节为准。 1. **建洞＝裸节点＋占位值＋零代填**：门洞 W/H/D 落占位默认值（400×400×20），**不解析邻板、不代填任何引用邻板的公式、不 seed PX/PY/PZ 位置参数桥**（`buildOpeningFormulas` 邻板引用与 `seedPanelFormulaParams` 整体退役）。洞口尺寸永远是普通可编辑值/公式，用户自己写（如 `W=#W-#bh*2`、`H=#H-#bh*2`）。 2. **门板跟随洞口（保留）**：门板收编后 `w=#W+盖法/缝值项`，改洞尺寸门板自动适配（酷家乐口径）；门板公式仍是普通可编辑公式。 3. **酷家乐门洞无厚度维**（官方《全卫参数化建模·门洞结构》："门洞设置不考虑厚度参数"）；本实现保留 D 作为可编辑值（默认=门板实测厚度，门板 `d=#D` 依赖），为登记过的偏离项。 4. **门洞新增「所在面」（正面/背面）**：不做只能做柜体正面门板；背面门板（如榻榻米背门）也要能建洞。 5. 下文用户故事 2/3/4/5、实现决策「ref 动态解析」、流程图「默认＝洞口净空公式」按本节修正后理解。 **Blocked by: #616**（轮廓表达式方言统一 v3）——按 2026-11-16 排期拍板，#616 落地后开工，避免新写的公式随即要迁移一遍。 **流程图**（有分支）： ## 问题（Problem Statement） 设计师装门板时，门板尺寸是手工数字或手写公式：柜体一改尺寸/板厚，门板不跟随，要重新量、重新算、重新填。酷家乐用「门洞＋关联门板」解决这个问题——门洞定洞口（净空、不含板厚），门板关联后自动变成洞口大小、移到洞口位置，柜体怎么改都自动跟随。我们没有这一层，等价能力只到「人手写公式」（如 `w=#W-@zcb.W-@zcb.W`），会写的人少、写错的没人拦。 ## 方案（Solution） 柜体树上新增「门洞」节点层：设计师选中门板右键「添加门洞」，一步完成建洞（默认代填洞口净空公式）＋门板收编为门洞子节点＋代填门板尺寸/位置/开门方向公式。之后改柜体尺寸或板厚，洞自动变、门板自动变，生产导出同步一致。门洞只存在于建模器：不进生产 JSON、不进报价，工厂拿到的仍是门板成品尺寸。 ## 用户故事（User Stories） 1. 作为橱柜设计师，我要选中门板后右键「添加门洞」，一步把门板套进门洞里，不用先建洞再找板关联。 2. 【2026-11-19 修正】作为橱柜设计师，建洞给我一个占位尺寸（400×400×20）就行，洞口尺寸/位置我自己在右栏改。 3. 【2026-11-19 修正】作为橱柜设计师，我要洞口 W/H/D 是普通可编辑值或公式，自己写 `W=#W-#bh*2` 这类跟柜体联动的公式，系统不代填、不引用邻板。 4. 【2026-11-19 作废】原「门洞公式引用实际板件」口径废弃——洞口公式由用户自写，系统不再解析邻板（撞内核 #448 同层唯一名规则，素材柜全撞 part1 重名）。 5. 【2026-11-19 作废】随故事 4 一并作废：不再解析邻板，此场景不存在。 6. 作为橱柜设计师，我要门板尺寸＝洞口＋盖法/缝值（按既有门板系统变量代填），与既有盖法体系一致不打架。 7. 作为橱柜设计师，我要门板位置自动落到门洞处（位置公式代填），不用手动对齐。 8. 作为橱柜设计师，我要门板开门方向由门洞的方向决定（关联时代填 KMFX），不会出现洞朝左门朝右。 9. 作为橱柜设计师，代填完的公式我要还能手工编辑，公式永远是普通可编辑公式。 10. 作为橱柜设计师，我要换绑：门洞右键「关联门板」换成另一块门板，旧板自动解绑。 11. 作为橱柜设计师，代填命中已有公式时，我要先收到「将覆盖」提示，确认后才写。 12. 作为橱柜设计师，我要在结构导航里看到「柜体→门洞→门板」层级，门洞在树上可见可选。 13. 作为橱柜设计师，删除门洞/解关联时我要门板自动降级回普通板件：位置不动、公式保留成普通公式，工作零损失。 14. 作为橱柜设计师，我要加错门洞能一步撤销（撤回到加之前的状态）。 15. 作为橱柜设计师，我要同一柜体上放多个门洞（如对开双门各占一洞），每个洞绑一块板。 16. 作为橱柜设计师，我要门洞在单元柜和组合柜里都能用（挂在对应柜体帧下）。 17. 作为橱柜设计师，我要保存后重开档案，门洞和关联关系原样还原，开档体检不报悬空。 18. 作为工厂/生产端，我要导出的生产 JSON 和报价里完全没有门洞，门板以成品尺寸出现在柜体层——拿到的东西和现在一模一样。 19. 作为商城端用户，我看到的柜子和以前一样（门洞不进商城可见数据），商城宿主零改动。 20. 作为维护者，我要门洞剪枝/提升复用阵列容器的既有采集模式，不新写第二份影子层机制。 21. 作为维护者，我要门洞不是参数透明层（门板 `#` 落到门洞、不跳过），既有透明机制零改动。 ## 实现决策（Implementation Decisions） - **门洞＝树上真节点容器**：携带真实宽/高/位置（非零变换）。与阵列容器的零变换纪律刻意不同——门洞是「身份容器保留真实 transform」型（筑木容器树已有此分型），不是「透明容器恒等 transform」型。 - **尺寸施加准入开新判据**：宿主建模层现有「容器禁止尺寸施加」的判

items.title: Ask HN: Where do you see Software in 5 years?
items.description: I wanted to hear some good opinions on all things AI and how they transform the Software industry. I'm anxious about the future and lack the foresight to form any opinion on what to do next. For context, I'm a L4 SWE that has more or less say 5-10 yrs of exp. I've enjoyed my work throughout my career, AI makes me ship more, much more than I could do 3 years ago. I feel I use it well and it translates into really good software. That said, what do you think happens in years to come with the Software industry in general? Do you think we'll go through a massive erosion of jobs? What's your perspective on that? I'm asking because I honestly don't know what to do: I can try to always keep up to date with newest technologies, best practices, but I'm only me; if the demand for SWEs and jobs falls to the floor, I'm not sure I'll always get a place at the table (i.e. land a job) and I'm wondering whether I should try to do something else in some other industry. It feels weird to be in a good position in life and still constantly worry about it getting worse.

items.title: Ask HN: If AI tools are so good, why isn't your bug backlog empty?
items.description: A lot of people outside tech ask me if AI is going to replace programmers and I just think: if that were the case we should be running out of things to do The bug backlog should be empty and we've caught up to every feature request from PMs to the point that we are bottlenecked on the business side But that does not seem to be the case with my own company or most devs I talk to in the industry So what gives?

items.title: Ask HN: When was the last time you thought "that's bad API design"?
items.description: I used to be irrationally impressed when I saw good API design and docs. Now I can't remember the last time I sat down and spent meaningful time reading docs for a platform. I've just gotten in the habit of pointing Claude at them or using a service like Context7 for the past year or so. As a consumer, I've realized that I'm not even sure which services I use that have good or badly designed APIs. If you maintain an API, have you changed how you write docs now that the main reader is probably an LLM?

items.title: Ask HN: When does your app need its own UI vs. using it via MCP?
